description: Three-panel composite figure mixing an optical micrograph (a) with two deep-etched SEM micrographs (b, c), all showing κ(j)-phase morphology in a 2Mn-8Al-0.2C (wt.%) alloy. (a) Grayscale optical micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar: several rounded/polygonal γ (austenite) particles sit in an α (ferrite) matrix, each γ outlined by a dark, scalloped, lobed rim labelled κ by an arrow. (b) SEM, deep etched, footer "Mag = 1.46 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV", 10 µm scale bar: a 3D ridge of κ-phase plates/laths growing from and roughly perpendicular to a flat central γ plate embedded in α, revealing the true three-dimensional, nonlamellar eutectoid morphology. (c) SEM, deep etched, footer "Mag = 2.00 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV", 10 µm scale bar: a hollow κ "cocoon" shell with an evacuated core inside α, the residue of fully decomposed austenite. No numeric property values are printed on any panel. The group argues that slow cooling from the two-phase domain precipitates κ at α/γ interfaces, that deep etching (b) exposes the κ ridge growing along the austenite long axis, and that isothermal treatment (c) decomposes austenite leaving only a κ cocoon.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an optical micrograph with a printed 20 µm scale bar; panel (b) and (c) are SEM micrographs each with a printed 10 µm scale bar and footer text 'Mag = 1.46 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV' and 'Mag = 2.00 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV' respectively.
In panel (a), γ (austenite) regions are enclosed by dark, scalloped/lobed rims that an arrow labels κ, all sitting inside an α (ferrite) matrix.
In panel (b), the κ-phase appears as plate-like laths growing outward from a flat, elongated γ plate, i.e. the κ growth is coupled to the austenite plate geometry.
In panel (c), the κ-phase forms a hollow shell (cocoon) around an empty core, with no γ remaining inside the shell.
Panel (a) shows the microstructure after cooling from 1400 °C at 10 °C/s and quenching at 870 °C.
Panel (b) is the same material as (a) but after a deep-etching procedure, and panel (c) is after 15 min at 870 °C followed by deep etching.

When cooling at low rates from the two-phase domain, the j-phase precipitates at the interface between austenite and ferrite, producing what the text calls a nonlamellar eutectoid with the j-phase and ferrite.
The three-dimensional morphology from deep etching shows the j-phase growing along the long axis of austenite.
At these low Mn contents, isothermal treatment in the two-phase ferrite–j-phase domain fully decomposes austenite, leaving a sort of cocoon of the j-phase.

sample_hints: cooled from 1400 °C at 10 °C/s and quenched at 870 °C

subfigures.description: Grayscale optical micrograph, 20 µm scale bar, showing rounded γ (austenite) particles in an α (ferrite) matrix; each γ is bordered by a dark scalloped/lobed κ rim (arrow). Straight polishing/scratch lines cross the α matrix.

Deep-etched SEM micrograph (Mag = 1.46 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV, 10 µm scale bar) showing a three-dimensional κ-phase ridge: plate-like laths emerging from and around a flat central γ plate embedded in the α matrix.

Deep-etched SEM micrograph (Mag = 2.00 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV, 10 µm scale bar) showing a hollow κ-phase 'cocoon' shell around an empty core in the α matrix, with κ indicated by arrow; a similar shell is partly visible at lower left.
